youtube.title: George Washington Never Had Wooden Teeth. Here's What They Were
youtube.description:
By his 1789 inauguration, George Washington had one natural tooth left. His dentures, according to Mount Vernon, which holds the only complete surviving set, combined hippopotamus and walrus ivory, cow and horse teeth, lead, brass, gold springs, and human teeth. In May 1784, nine teeth were bought from enslaved people at Mount Vernon on Washington's account; historians can't say whether those exact teeth went into his dentures. The wooden-teeth myth may come from stained ivory, which can look like grained wood.
